body.body:
**Ready for review (Sean approved moving it out of draft at `55a1e720`). Lane CC1-B, Trust Harness gate P1A "Inspect". Do not merge, publish or version-bump without Sean's approval.**

The standard this PR is held to: **TrustShell must never claim more than its evidence can prove.**

## Round 8 (XC1 re-check 5 of `f70b33c1`): what changed in `55a1e720`

XC1 found **no new finding against the property**. Every earlier probe was re-run clean. Two low items and one usability note:

- **W2 (low, was exit 0). A GitHub URL had no host boundary.** `agithub.com/…/runs/<id>` was SUPPORTED, because the match began at `github.com` inside the longer host name.
  - Run and commit links now start at a host boundary.
  - `github.com` and `www.github.com` still count.
  - A longer host name or a subdomain is unread, so it blocks the text.
- **Byte-order mark (usability).** Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes a BOM for `Out-File` and `Set-Content -Encoding utf8`. It made line 1 non-ASCII, so a claims file written from that shell could never decide.
  - `--claims-file` now drops **one** leading BOM, and only that one.
- **W1 (low), not changed: a `Locally` paragraph above a claim.**
  - The claim's verdict stays within its own scope: whether the cited run passed. That is what the record establishes.
  - The `Locally` paragraph is listed as a NOT_CHECKED local-run claim.
  - The text exits 3.

**Tests:** the three W2 inputs are in the regression corpus. There are direct tests for the host boundary (with `github.com` and `www.github.com` controls) and for the BOM, both unit and end to end.

## Round 7 (XC1 re-check 4 of `466dff84`): what changed in `366d59fa` and `f70b33c1`

XC1 re-ran every earlier probe on `466dff84`, and all of them are closed; X9 is now CONTRADICTED, exit 1. XC1 found one way the stated property fails, and two citations that identified less than they appeared to:

- **Y1 (medium). GitHub renders adjacent lines as one paragraph.** "Locally" on the line above a claim, or "locally." on the line below, turned the rendered claim into a local-run claim, but the line itself stayed SUPPORTED (exit 3).
  - **Now each claim must be its own paragraph.** Two non-blank lines with no blank line between them block every verdict in the text.
  - **A line holding only a no-break space is no longer blank.** CommonMark treats it as a paragraph line. It is non-ASCII, so it blocks the text.
- **Z1 (medium, was exit 0). A workflow display name is not unique.** "The check workflow passed on 5cd68edc" was SUPPORTED by any run whose `name:` is `check`, and two workflow files can share one name.
  - **`gha.run_succeeded` now needs the run id.**
  - A workflow name, if the line gives one, must still match.
  - A commit alone, or a name plus a commit, is NOT_CHECKED.
- **Z2 (medium-low, was exit 0). A 7-hex SHA prefix is 28 bits, and a matching commit can be ground.**
  - **A SHA citation now supports only at 12 or more hex characters** (48 bits).
  - A shorter citation that matches is NOT_CHECKED, and the reason says why.
  - A mismatch of any length is still CONTRADICTED.
- **Y3 (low, was exit 0).** "That the check workflow passed in run …" is a fragment, not an assertion. "that" is no longer a filler word, so the line has unread words and blocks the text.

**Tests and fixtures:**
- All six inputs are in the regression corpus, where none may give exit 0 or a SUPPORTED outcome. Each rule also has its own direct test.
- The fixtures, demo claims and docs now put a blank line between claims and use 12-character SHAs.

**Card wording** (`f70b33c1`): the `git.head_sha` scope line said "A short SHA is matched as a prefix". It now states the 12-character minimum.

**Not adopted:** XC1's informational `:a:` note. The shortcode renders as an emoji, but no shortcode built only from filler words negates anything, so the claim does not change.

## Round 6: deny by default (design correction from the coordinating session), in `466dff84`

XC1's third re-check (X1–X9 at `4536e199`) broke the strict-subset reader again, using only modelled constructs:
- canonicalisation ran before structure, so fullwidth or zero-width comment delimiters hid lines;
- `<!-->` was not ended on its own line;
- a list marker plus 5 spaces is code;
- a link definition label, or a link title, can span two lines;
- a paragraph of inline code was certified;
- "2." cannot interrupt a paragraph;
- a same-id URL in another repo was dropped.

The bypass count across rounds was 6, then 4, then 6: not converging. Every gap came from re-implementing what a reader of rendered Markdown sees, which the brief never asked for. (The X1–X9 fixes to that reader are kept in history as the verified checkpoint `fd871028`.)

**The reader is gone.** Nothing is rendered or normalised before a decision:
- **Only plain claim lines are read.** Each must be printable ASCII, start with a letter, contain none of ``< > ` [ ] ( ) | * _ # ~ \ $ & { } ?``, hold one sentence, and be at most 200 characters.
- **Any other line is listed as written** (cleaned for display only), as `excluded.markup`, NOT_CHECKED, with its line number.
- **One line that is not plain, or not read end to end, blocks every verdict in the text.** That covers a Markdown line, "That is false.", a cross mark, or "Has the …". Everything is still listed, and the reason names the first blocking line.
- **A PR description written in Markdown is therefore NOT_CHECKED as a whole.** To be checked, claims are written as plain lines. This is the brief's own fallback: deterministic templates, and anything else NOT_CHECKED.
- **Every XC1 input from all four rounds** (about 50) is a regression case. None may yield exit 0 or a SUPPORTED outcome, on a green run or a red one.
- **Kept unchanged:** the templates, the JCS hash, the card and the fixtures. The fixtures' claim files are rewritten as plain lines.

## Round 5 (XC1 re-check 2 of `12fd3c79`): what changed in `4536e199`

XC1 confirmed rule 2 (the allow-list) holds, apart from one gap in question detection, and that every earlier finding stays closed. Rule 1 did not hold: the hand-written Markdown reader mis-modelled several constructs. Soft line breaks, a comment inside indented code or a fence info string, a fence "closed" outside its list or quote, link reference definitions, image alt text and setext headings each hid visible text or certified an example, three of them at exit 0. Patching each construct is a losing game, so the reader is now **correct by construction** instead:

- **A strict subset is read exactly:** paragraphs (soft line breaks joined, as GitHub renders them), list items with continuation lines, task boxes, ATX headings, fences opened at column 0, and whole-line HTML comment blocks (column 0, ending a line with `-->`).
- **Anything outside the subset refuses the whole text.** That covers:
  - blockquotes, any other `<`, images, link definitions and titles, tables, footnotes;
  - setext underlines and rules, tab indentation, indented code, fences inside a list;
  - unclosed comments, or text after `-->`.

  Every line is still listed, and the reason names the construct and line, but **nothing in the text is decided**. A parsing mistake can now never hide visible text or certify an example; at worst it refuses text it could have read.
- **A verdict needs its whole paragraph read end to end.** This closes R1-a ("… (run N). ❌", a lone "?" on the next line) and R1-b ("… (run N)\nis false.").
- **Questions after leading emphasis or a connective** ("*Has* the …", "And is CI green …") are now detected.
- **A citation repeated in one sentence** (link text plus URL) counts as read, so the sentence isn't gated for repeating itself.
- **T-a.** `- [ ]text` with no space is a to-do.

What still decides in a typical PR description: plain paragraphs and list items. A template's HTML comment block is fine; a blockquote, image or table anywhere makes the whole text NOT_CHECKED.

## Round 4 (XC1 re-check of `be80f012`): what changed in `12fd3c79`

XC1 confirmed every round-3 finding closed (`xc1-recheck-pr583.md`), then found new ways round the fixes. All of them reproduced before the fix, and each has a regression test. Patching each case one at a time is how these kept slipping through, so this round changes two underlying rules instead:

**1. Drop only what a reader cannot see; decide only plain statements.**
- HTML comments are now the only thing removed: block comments, and inline ones outside code spans (N9: a claim inside an inline comment was SUPPORTED although no reader sees it).
- Everything else a reader sees is **listed, with its context, and decides nothing**: headings, fenced code, indented code (N8), blockquotes including lazy continuation lines (N6), and unticked to-dos.
- Fences are now found inside list items too (N4: `- ```` was missed, its closing line opened a new fence, and a visible "the deploy workflow failed" line vanished at exit 0).
- So a parsing mistake can only make something NOT_CHECKED. It can never hide visible text, or certify an example.

**2. Leftover words are judged by an allow-list, not a deny-list.**
- A leftover says nothing only if it is whitespace, plain ASCII punctuation, emphasis or code marks, and a short list of filler words. Everything else is unread meaning:
  - `~` (N1: `~~…~~` strikethrough is a retraction, and it was exit 0);
  - any symbol or emoji (N2: ❌ ✗ 🚫 negate);
  - non-ASCII question marks (N3: ‽ ؟ ⸮);
  - possessives (N7: "My checks pass" is not "all checks").
- A sentence opening with an auxiliary verb is a question (N5: "Has the check workflow passed (run N)." was exit 0 on green and CONTRADICTED on red).

**Also:**
- **N10.** `--json` and `record.json` now write C1 controls, bidi and invisible characters as JSON unicode escapes. It's the same JSON value, so the digest is unchanged.

## Round 3 (XC1 adversarial review of `7c16dc22`): what changed in `be80f012`

XC1's report is `xc1-review-pr583.md` in the shared side-session notes folder. I reproduced every finding against the `7c16dc22` build before fixing it, and each now has a regression test named after its id.

**Exit-0 overclaims (all fixed):**
- **F7.** "The workflow passed on 5cd68edc" was SUPPORTED by whichever green workflow ran on that commit, for example an always-green labeler. `gha.run_succeeded` now needs the **run id**, or the **workflow's own name plus the commit**.
- **F1.** "attempt 1" alone tied a sentence to the run. An attempt now never ties anything; it can only break a tie.
- **H1.** A line starting with ```` ```x``` ```` was taken as a fence, and every later line vanished. Fences now follow CommonMark: a backtick fence's info string can't contain a backtick, and a fence closes only on the same character, at least as long.

**Visible text dropped (fixed):**
- **H2.** A `<!--` inside a code span deleted later lines. Only a comment **block** (a line starting with `<!--`, through `-->`) is removed now. Mid-line or unclosed `<!--` is text.

**SUPPORTED next to a sentence that says otherwise (about 15 cases, fixed by one rule):**
- **R1, generalised.** A sentence decides nothing (every part NOT_CHECKED) unless the templates read it end to end, and it isn't a question or a blockquote.
  - This covers conditionals, "unclear whether", a negation smuggled in with invisible characters, a "deploy" workflow name in quotes, emphasis or parentheses, "dry run", "rebased on <sha>", "first try", "lint checks" and "required checks", and questions.
  - Ties are per sentence, with no text-level fallback.
  - Remainders are counted in any script.
- **Normalisation first.** Text is normalised once, then every template reads it and every card shows it in that same form. Invisible characters are stripped (soft hyphen, U+2060–206F, variation selectors, tag block and more), NFKC is applied (fullwidth digits become digits), and controls become spaces. A reader can't see a word the checks didn't.

**Overstated CONTRADICTED (fixed by R1):**
- **G1/G2.** "Lint checks" or "required checks" against a red run.
- **G3.** A question followed by a denial.

**Security:**
- **S1.** A workflow or job name carrying terminal escapes (OSC 52 clipboard write, clear-screen) reached the stdout card. Every card string now passes one control/invisible filter, and the raw value stays in the record, where JSON escapes it.
- **S2.** `--claims <file|text>` read a local file whenever the "text" was a path, so `--claims "$PR_BODY"` could leak `.env`. It is now **`--claims "<text>"`, always text**, and **`--claims-file <path>`**, the only file read.
- **S3.** `excluded.test_count` was quadratic: `1,1,1,…` took about 2 minutes at the 256 KiB limit. It is now bounded. The timing tests add those shapes, plus every pair of units.
- **L1.** An unpaired surrogate from GitHub made the digest throw. It becomes U+FFFD when GitHub's data is read in.
- **L2.** The not-checked heading counts what its list holds.
- **L4.** A job with no `head_sha` is no longer tied to the commit.

**Not changed here:**
- L3 (blockquotes) is covered by R1.
- XC1 noted that plain `check <url>`'s `formatCheckCard` prints `run.body.name` raw. That predates this PR; it's left as a follow-up to keep this PR on P1A.

**Re-review:** XC1 re-ran its probes on `be80f012` and confirmed every round-3 finding closed (round 4 above).

## Round 2 (Sean's review of `b5af246f`): what changed

1. **CodeQL `js/polynomial-redos` (alert #26, high): valid, and fixed.** The rule flagged `src/lib/action-evidence.ts:151`, the HTML-comment stripper `/<!--[\s\S]*?-->/g`. On text made of repeated `<!--` with no `-->`, it rescans to the end from every opener. Measured: 8 K characters took 23 ms; 16 K, 90 ms; 32 K, 388 ms; 64 K, 1,694 ms. Each doubling is roughly 4×, so the 256 KiB `--claims` limit costs about 27 s. It was replaced by a one-pass `indexOf` loop (`stripHtmlComments`), checked against the old regex on 2,000 seeded random strings for an identical result. Timing the rest of the file found **three more patterns of the same shape that CodeQL did not flag**: `\s*` + optional + `\s*` in the commit, run and attempt citations. `"commit"` + 80 K spaces took **130 s**; `run` took 38 s; `attempt` took 31 s. All were rewritten. A fifth candidate I nearly introduced (a `[…]+$` trim) is now a loop. Every template is timed against 26 hostile keywords × 4 shapes × 50 K characters in the test suite. In the local benchmark, the worst of 148 inputs of 100 K characters takes 35 ms.
2. **Evidence accuracy: SUPPORTED narrowed, and claims made atomic.**
   - Each claim is split into atomic parts with separate verdicts. A record entry now has `claim` (the exact span) and `sentence` (its source). Whatever a sentence says that no template matched becomes its own `unmapped` NOT_CHECKED entry, so a green citation can't sit next to an unread "CI is not green".
   - A successful run supports exactly one outcome: **`gha.run_succeeded`**, "this workflow run succeeded". It needs conclusion success, every job read, at least one job run, and all jobs on this commit and attempt.
   - **`ci.tests_pass`** ("all tests pass") is **never SUPPORTED and never CONTRADICTED** by a run record. A green run doesn't say which tests ran, and a red run doesn't say a test failed.
   - **`ci.all_checks_pass`** ("all checks pass", "CI is green") is **never SUPPORTED** by one run. A failed run or failed job can CONTRADICT it, since one failing check is a counterexample.
   - "The fix works", "production ready", "secure" and similar claims stay NOT_CHECKED.
   - **Two more overclaims found by probing, and fixed:**
     - "The **deploy** workflow passed on 5cd68edc", paired with the `check` run, was SUPPORTED. The workflow name is now captured and must match the run's display name or file stem, otherwise NOT_CHECKED; the claimant's name is never spliced into generated text.
     - "The **job** passed" was read as the whole run succeeding. A job is not the run, so that phrasing no longer maps to `gha.run_succeeded`.
     - A `completed` run with a null or unrecognised conclusion now gives NOT_CHECKED, not CONTRADICTED.
   - **Tie rule:** an outcome is compared only when the text ties it to the inspected run. The sentence must cite this run's commit or run id, with nothing cited that doesn't match; or, for an uncited sentence, the whole text must. Otherwise the outcome is NOT_CHECKED. A green run is never evidence for a sentence about another commit, and an uncited "the workflow passed" next to an unrelated green run is NOT_CHECKED.
3. **Baseline: the six Windows suite failures also occur on clean `main`.** I made a temporary detached worktree of `origin/main` (`5cd68edc`) with `core.autocrlf=true` and its own `npm ci`, and ran the six suites. **6 of 6 suites fail, with the same 7 tests and the same errors** (schema hash `4ffe1635…`, `\n`-anchored workflow regexes, the doubled Windows path, the spawn of `C:\Program Files\…`). So they are pre-existing in this environment and not caused by this PR. The worktree was removed afterwards. **Ubuntu CI is authoritative for this PR:** on `b5af246f`, `check` (tsc + jest), `Analyze (javascript-typescript)`, gitleaks, receipt, verify-paris and Vercel passed. `CodeQL` failed only on alert #26.

## What this adds (unchanged from round 1 unless noted)

`trustshell check <runUrl> --claims "<text>"` (or `--claims-file <path>`), with claims written as plain lines: reads a public GitHub Actions run and what an agent *said* about it, then gives each atomic claim a verdict against what the run *reports*.

- **Built on `src/lib/check.ts`, not a rewrite.** The only change there is additive: `runCheck` also returns the raw `run` and `jobs` facts its verdict was already computed from. Verdicts, exit codes and card are unchanged; `check --json` gains those two fields.
- **Egress: api.github.com only**, the same two requests as `check <runUrl>`. No model, no backend. `scripts/check-egress.cjs` runs the `--claims` path with the network stubbed (only api.github.com is reached, and nothing at all under `OFFLINE=1`).
- **Record** `dev.trustshell.action-evidence/0.1-draft`, exactly five members: `schema`, `observation`, `claims[]`, `assurance` (`cryptographic_integrity: NOT_CHECKED`, `observation: PLATFORM_REPORTED`), `does_not_prove[]`. Its digest is SHA-256 over RFC 8785 (`src/lib/jcs.ts`, which is strict and tested against the RFC's own vectors; it is not the engine-pinned `kernelCanonicalJson`, which writes NaN as `null`, drops `undefined` and escapes lone surrogates).
- **Card**, Markdown and HTML, rendered from the record alone. Every NOT_CHECKED claim has its own line. Foreign text appears only in code spans or escaped HTML. The HTML has CSP `default-src 'none'` and no script.
- **Exit codes:** 0 when every claim is SUPPORTED on a COMPLETE run; 1 when a claim is CONTRADICTED or the run FAILED or is INCONSISTENT; 3 when anything is NOT_CHECKED.
- Reference: `docs/action-evidence.md`, which includes the full template table.

## Fixtures and tests

Real api.github.com responses for trustshell's own `check` runs: `green-run.json` (39290226738) and `failed-run.json` (39166529852), both unmodified, plus `no-jobs.json`, derived and labelled as such. Further shapes are derived inline and named where they're made.

Scenarios covered: a green run with narrow claims (all SUPPORTED, exit 0); a misleading green run ("all tests pass, all checks pass, the fix works": none SUPPORTED); claims not tied to the run; another commit; a run id in another repo; a wrong SHA; a wrong attempt (run and attempt get separate verdicts); missing evidence (no jobs, 404, truncated list, in progress, all skipped, a job on another commit, a green run with a failed job); a failed run (contradicts "the workflow passed" and "all checks pass", never "all tests pass"); a cancelled run; an overclaiming PR description; negated and partial phrasing; hostile Markdown and HTML; lines with no blank line between them; SHA prefixes shorter than 12 characters; a workflow named with a commit but no run id; and ReDoS timing. An invariant test asserts over a corpus, on both runs, that only citations and `gha.run_succeeded` are ever SUPPORTED, and the latter only on a COMPLETE success run.

## Test results
Ran locally on `55a1e720` (Windows 11, Node 22.17.0, repo-pinned TypeScript 5.9.3 from `node_modules`):

- `tsc --noEmit` (root tsconfig, the CI gate): **exit 0**.
- The four claim suites (`tests/action-evidence.test.ts`, `tests/cli-check-claims.test.ts`, `tests/jcs.test.ts`, existing `tests/check.test.ts`): **345 tests passed**. These include the XC1 regression corpus: every input from six rounds, none giving exit 0 or a SUPPORTED outcome.
- `node scripts/check-egress.cjs`: **VERIFIED**. Only api.github.com is reached, including for `--claims`, and nothing at all under `OFFLINE=1`.
- `node scripts/check-doc-version.cjs`: **VERIFIED**.
- Full `npm run verify` on `55a1e720`: **284 of 290 suites; 4794 tests passed, 7 failed, 2 skipped.** The 7 failures are exactly the ones that also fail on a clean `main` checkout (`5cd68edc`) on this machine (round 2, item 3).
- **Ubuntu CI is authoritative.** On every head since `7c16dc22` (`be80f012`, `12fd3c79`, `4536e199`, `466dff84`, `366d59fa`, `f70b33c1`), all 9 checks passed, **including CodeQL**. There are **0 open code-scanning alerts** on the PR. CI for `55a1e720` is running.

## Real example: SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED and NOT_CHECKED (DEMO)
The run is real: trustshell's own `check` run [39290226738](https://github.com/DealAppSeo/trustshell/actions/runs/39290226738), read live and anonymously by the built CLI at 2026-10-20T01:59:44.971Z. The claims text is **illustrative**, written for the demo, one claim per paragraph:

```
Done.

The check workflow passed on 5cd68edc782f, run 39290226738.

CI passed on attempt 2.

All tests pass.

It is production ready and fully secure.
```

Result: exit 1.
- **SUPPORTED:** `The check workflow passed`, `on 5cd68edc782f`, `run 39290226738`.
- **CONTRADICTED:** `attempt 2`.
- **NOT_CHECKED:** `Done`, `CI passed`, `All tests pass`, `production ready`, `fully secure`, and cryptographic integrity.

The record digest `9f3f779dedbfa2a2f9aca2f2ce8794b6ca8b24b8e243f7a884079bad49eded03` was recomputed independently in Python and matches. Files: `examples/action-evidence-demo/{record.json,card.md,card.html}`. Sean picks the official run later.

<details><summary>card.md</summary>

> **DEMO.** Sample output for review, generated from a real public GitHub Actions run. Not an official TrustShell result.

## TrustShell · claims checked against a GitHub Actions run

- **Run** `DealAppSeo/trustshell` · run 39290226738 · attempt 1 · commit `5cd68edc782fb2dd74e343e9335d3a8bcb04d5e5`
- **Workflow** `check` · `.github/workflows/check.yml`
- **GitHub reports** status `completed` · conclusion `success` · check verdict **COMPLETE**
- **Jobs** 1 of 1 read (HTTP 200): 1 success
- **Observed** 2026-10-20T01:59:44.971Z from api.github.com (LIVE at that time)
- **Evidence class** PLATFORM_REPORTED: GitHub describing its own run. A platform record, not an independent grade.

### Claims: 3 supported · 1 contradicted · 5 not checked

- **CONTRADICTED** `attempt 2`
  - **In** `CI passed on attempt 2.`
  - **Template** `gha.run_attempt`
  - **Why** The claim cites attempt 2; GitHub's record for run 39290226738 is attempt 1, its latest.
  - **Scope** Attempt identity only: whether the attempt this claim cites is the one GitHub's record describes. Not what that attempt shows.
  - **Fields** `/observation/run_attempt`
- **SUPPORTED** `The check workflow passed`
  - **In** `The check workflow passed on 5cd68edc782f, run 39290226738.`
  - **Template** `gha.run_succeeded`
  - **Why** GitHub reports conclusion "success" for run 39290226738 (attempt 1, commit 5cd68edc782f); 1 of 1 job concluded success. The line cites this run.
  - **Scope** Whether workflow run 39290226738 (attempt 1, commit 5cd68edc782f) concluded success with every job read. Not which tests it ran, not any other workflow or check on the commit, and not whether the change works.
  - **Fields** `/observation/status`, `/observation/conclusion`, `/observation/check/verdict`, `/observation/jobs`
- **SUPPORTED** `on 5cd68edc782f`
  - **In** `The check workflow passed on 5cd68edc782f, run 39290226738.`
  - **Template** `git.head_sha`
  - **Why** The inspected run's head_sha 5cd68edc782f begins with 5cd68edc782f.
  - **Scope** Commit identity only: whether the commit this claim cites is the one the inspected run ran on. A SHA is matched as a prefix, and a match supports only at 12 or more hex characters. Not what the commit changes or fixes.
  - **Fields** `/observation/head_sha`
- **SUPPORTED** `run 39290226738`
  - **In** `The check workflow passed on 5cd68edc782f, run 39290226738.`
  - **Template** `gha.run_id`
  - **Why** The cited run is the inspected run, 39290226738.
  - **Scope** Run identity only: whether the run this claim cites is the inspected run. Not what the run shows.
  - **Fields** `/observation/owner`, `/observation/repo`, `/observation/run_id`

### Not checked: 5 claims, and cryptographic integrity (none of these is a pass)

- **Task completion: not checked.** `Done` "Done" is not a fact a workflow run records. Only the narrower claims mapped from the same text are compared. In: `Done.`
- **All checks on the commit passing: not checked.** `CI passed` This sentence cites a commit, run or attempt that is not, or could not be matched to, the inspected run, so its outcome claims are not compared with this run. In: `CI passed on attempt 2.`
- **Tests passing: not checked.** `All tests pass` This sentence cites neither this run's commit nor its run id, so nothing ties the claim to run 39290226738 (attempt 1, commit 5cd68edc782f). In: `All tests pass.`
- **Production readiness: not checked.** `production ready` Readiness is a judgement, not something a workflow run reports. In: `It is production ready and fully secure.`
- **Broader security: not checked.** `fully secure` A CI run conclusion is not a security review, and no security result is mapped. In: `It is production ready and fully secure.`
- **Cryptographic integrity: not checked.** No signed attestation was present or verified. This version does not read attestations.

### What this does not prove

- This is what GitHub can confirm. It is not a judgement about whether the code is correct.
- It cannot show work done outside this repository, or on a branch that was never pushed.
- A passing test suite proves the tests that exist passed — not that the right tests exist.
- It does not establish who or what authored the change.
- SUPPORTED means the platform record matches the narrow scope written next to the claim. It is not a finding that the claim is true in any broader sense.
- A successful workflow run shows that run succeeded. It does not show which tests ran, that all tests or all checks passed, or that a change works.
- Only this one workflow run was read. Other workflows, check suites and status checks on the same commit were not.
- Every observed fact is GitHub reporting on its own run (PLATFORM_REPORTED). Nothing was re-run or independently observed.
- Broader security: not checked. A CI conclusion is not a security review.
- The record is not signed. Its SHA-256 shows whether the record changed after it was made, not who made it.

## Remaining limitations (by design in this version)
- **Cryptographic integrity:** no attestation (e.g. GitHub artifact attestations or Sigstore) is read or verified.
- **"All tests pass" is never decided.** That would need test reports or step-level logs, which aren't read.
- **"All checks pass" is never SUPPORTED.** Only one workflow run is read, not every check run on the commit.
- **Markdown is not read at all.** Only plain claim lines decide, and any Markdown or non-ASCII line blocks every verdict in the text. A Markdown PR description is NOT_CHECKED as a whole, though every line is listed. Reading GitHub's own rendering (the PR body as HTML through api.github.com) is a possible next step, not in this PR.
- **Each claim must be its own paragraph.** Lines with no blank line between them render as one paragraph on GitHub, so they decide nothing.
- **"This workflow passed" needs the run id.** A commit alone, or a workflow name plus a commit, is NOT_CHECKED: a commit has many runs, and two workflow files can share a display name.
- **Run and commit links count only on `github.com` or `www.github.com`.**
- **A SHA citation supports only at 12 or more hex characters.** A shorter matching prefix is NOT_CHECKED; a mismatch is CONTRADICTED at any length.
- **Claim recognition is a fixed phrase set, and it is strict.** Unrecognised phrasings fall to `unmapped` NOT_CHECKED and are never SUPPORTED. A sentence with *any* unread word decides nothing, so natural prose often gets NOT_CHECKED where a person might decide it. That is deliberate, and the price of never overclaiming.
- **Ties come from each sentence's own citations.** A bare SHA with no context word ("Pushed deadbeef1") is not read as a citation. It shows up as unread words instead, so that sentence decides nothing.
- **Artifacts, coverage, test counts, deployment, performance and reviews** are not read.
- **Earlier attempts:** GitHub's run endpoint answers for the latest attempt. In `--claims`, a URL naming an earlier attempt is refused. Plain `check <url>/attempts/N`, which already existed, still reports the latest attempt without saying so.

## Does not prove
- What GitHub can confirm is not a judgement about whether the code is correct.
- It cannot show work done outside this repository, or on a branch that was never pushed.
- A passing suite proves the tests that exist passed, not that the right tests exist.
- It does not establish who or what authored the change.
- SUPPORTED means the platform record establishes the claim within the scope written next to it, and nothing broader.
- A successful run shows that run succeeded. It does not show which tests ran, that all tests or checks passed, or that a change works.
- Every observed fact is GitHub reporting on its own run (PLATFORM_REPORTED). Nothing was re-run or independently observed.
- The record is not signed. Its hash shows whether it changed after it was made, not who made it.

## Design questions (noted, not adopted)
1. Align the record later with Agent Receipts, Obsigna or an in-toto Statement, so it can travel in DSSE/Sigstore envelopes. No dependency added.
2. Use GitHub artifact attestations (on api.github.com) as the path to a `cryptographic_integrity` other than NOT_CHECKED. Needs Sigstore bundle verification.
3. Read `/commits/{sha}/check-runs` so "all checks pass" could be SUPPORTED across every check on the commit.
4. Any NOT_CHECKED gives exit 3, consistent with the repo rule that NOT_CHECKED never shares a code with success. A gate may want a "fail only on CONTRADICTED" mode; that's Sean's call.
